newsitem.title: USA: N.J. budget to rely on $3.4 bln bond sale -- paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. budget to rely on $3.4 bln bond sale -- paper.

text.p: New Jersey Gov Christine Whitman plans to ask lawmakers to approve a $3.4 billion pension obligation bond sale as part of her fiscal 1998 budget proposal, the Sunday Star Ledger reported.
The state plans to borrow the money as part of a plan to shore up the state pension fund, freeing up pension surpluses to help pay the state's share of annual contributions into the fund.

Debt service in the first year of the plan would amount to $113 million, on top of current debt service of $453 million. But savings to the general fund total $623 million over the next two years, the paper said.
The deal, which Whitman administration officials said would be the largest single state bond sale in history, would take place before the end of the 1997 fiscal year on June 30.
